changes: weekday: 'roja 7' interpreted as Saturday (7th day counting from Sunday); kept the original wording in brackets

notes: added that 'saṃvat 1871' does not agree with Śaka 1793 if read as VS (VS 1871 = c. 1814 CE, whereas Śaka 1793 = VS 1928); it agrees only if read as the CE year. Also noted that it sits oddly inside the text and is placed before the verses, not in the final colophon

notes: The colophon names no persons. The final dating is Śaka 1793 Bhādra vadi 11, roja 7 (Saturday), which is 1871 CE. The 'saṃvat 1871' that comes earlier, inside the text, does not agree with this date if it is read as Vikrama: VS 1871 would be about 1814 CE, while Śaka 1793 is VS 1928. It agrees only if it is read as the Christian year 1871, which is unusual but possible in a late manuscript. Another possibility is that it belongs to an earlier exemplar, or is a stray marginal number that got copied into the text. The catalogue's 'SAM 1871' and 'ŚS 1793' therefore point to the same year only if SAM means CE. I took the Śaka date as authoritative.
